newsitem.title: USA: N.Y.C. Water board sees $41 mln surplus for 1996.
newsitem.headline: N.Y.C. Water board sees $41 mln surplus for 1996.

text.p: The New York City Municipal Water Finance Authority on Thursday said that it expects its 1996 surplus to be almost $41 million, slightly higher than expected, according to its preliminary financial report.
The statement, which was released at an investor conference held by the utility, showed that it expected to exceed its forecast by about $4.6 million.

Valerie Mehallow, the Authority's comptroller, said that she did not anticipate that the final financial report, which should be completed shortly, will differ substantially from the preliminary numbers.
"I don't believe there will any changes to that," she said, adding that she anticipated any modifications would be limited to perhaps a couple thousand of dollars here or there on some of the lines.

Operating revenues are expected to be around $1.142 billion, about $3.6 million more than expected. Payments from water and sewer users should run around $24.7 million, just over $4 million more than projected.
And interest income on Authority and Board funds is anticipated at around $1.167 billion, about $7.8 million more than projected.
